releasePosition: Atom63 remains a public beta, not a stable/latest contract.

dimensions.label: Package/install ergonomics and published tarball hygiene

benchmarkSignals.signal: Provides a short package install, a single global CSS import, and a root Theme setup.
Documents package installation, CSS import, and root Theme placement as one first-use path.
Documents the core package, theme package, required peer dependencies, and precompiled CSS distribution together.

dimensions.atom63Status: Package manifests, export maps, packed contents, and a local packed-consumer smoke are audited in CI. A clean install/build against the public registry after the next approved publish is not yet recorded.
gaps: Run a clean external registry install/build smoke after an approved beta publish.
Confirm the install path works without workspace overrides.
dimensions.nextAction: Record a clean external consumer install, import, CSS, render, and production-build smoke using only registry packages.

dimensions.label: Root/subpath API stability and preview/experimental policy

benchmarkSignals.signal: Keeps preview components in separately named preview packages and excludes them from the stable suite until promotion.
Uses a dedicated helper subpath for a large generated emoji-color lookup instead of expanding the package root.
Treats changes to public theme tokens as breaking changes.

dimensions.atom63Status: The root and public subpaths are inventoried, support tiers are machine-readable, and a preview subpath plus migration guidance exist. The beta root is still broader than the intended stable contract.
gaps: Resolve every P0 root family and public subpath decision.
Approve stable root narrowing without changing the beta root in this slice.
dimensions.nextAction: Complete the P0 stable action matrix and approve which APIs move to preview, remain stable, or become private.

dimensions.label: Dependency/peer/version policy

benchmarkSignals.signal: Declares React 19+ as a peer requirement and versions its public packages together through a Changesets fixed group.
Tests cross-React compatibility and uses an explicit release lifecycle for preview and stable packages.
Maintains installable packages in a public monorepo with release notes and migration documentation.

dimensions.atom63Status: React peers and first-wave package relationships are declared, and a Base UI incompatibility is pinned for beta. There is no complete policy for type-visible dependencies, supported React ranges, coordinated versions, or stable semver changes.
gaps: Define ownership and update rules for type-visible runtime dependencies.
Define supported React versions and a compatibility test matrix.
Define stable semver and coordinated-package version policy.
dimensions.nextAction: Publish a dependency and version policy, then add compatibility checks for every supported React and type-visible dependency range.

dimensions.label: Token/theme contract and CSS entry clarity

benchmarkSignals.signal: Exposes the CSS variables that power components and documents theme configuration as the supported customization contract.
Documents one global stylesheet import and a Theme root as the minimum setup.
Ships precompiled CSS and theme packages whose CSS custom properties customize the system without requiring StyleX in consumer builds.

dimensions.atom63Status: Token ownership, semantic roles, theme attributes, component contracts, CSS subpaths, and compatibility adapters are documented and covered by generated/token tests.
dimensions.nextAction: Keep token generation, CSS entry points, and authored theme-contract tests green through stable promotion.

dimensions.label: Component accessibility/interaction evidence

benchmarkSignals.signal: Builds on primitives that follow WAI-ARIA patterns and test focus management, keyboard navigation, browsers, and assistive technologies.
Requires behavior, keyboard, focus, ARIA, conformance, E2E, SSR, and cross-React test layers.
Publishes component accessibility guidance and a formal accessibility conformance report for its docs experience.

dimensions.atom63Status: Unit tests and partial evidence packets exist, but high-risk form, media, portal, motion, and overlay families still lack the required browser, mobile, keyboard, and assistive-technology evidence.
gaps: Complete real-browser keyboard, focus, pointer, touch, and reduced-motion checks for high-risk families.
Record screen-reader and mobile assistive-technology evidence for stable candidates.
Resolve every monitor-high-risk stable decision.
dimensions.nextAction: Execute the monitor evidence matrix in real browsers and assistive technology, then record pass/fail evidence per family.

dimensions.label: Examples/adopter smoke

benchmarkSignals.signal: Pairs package documentation with a getting-started path and tutorials that exercise the system in real app workflows.
Maintains example apps, a documentation site, Storybook, and a sandbox alongside published packages.
Links Storybook, a Figma kit, and source from its package entry and documents runnable first-use setup.

dimensions.atom63Status: A Vite example builds in CI, packed packages are smoke-tested locally, and an adopter branch has beta evidence. The main adopter still defaults to workspace packages and the clean registry-only path is not continuously proven.
gaps: Keep the product adopter green without root dependency overrides.
Add a repeatable registry-only consumer smoke after publish.
dimensions.nextAction: Promote the published-package adopter path to a repeatable smoke and record a clean registry-only build before stable.

dimensions.label: Docs IA / first-use quickstart

benchmarkSignals.signal: Presents installation, CSS import, Theme setup, customization, and component docs in a short ordered path.
Separates design resources, development resources, tutorials, foundations, and component guidance in its getting-started IA.
Organizes guidance into getting started, foundations, UI patterns, components, accessibility, and contribution routes.

dimensions.atom63Status: A public quickstart now links beta installation, CSS imports, theme and mode attributes, a first component, preview policy, verification, and next-step references. Full component, accessibility, and governance documentation IA is not yet stable-complete.
gaps: Add navigable component reference documentation for the stable candidate surface.
Add public accessibility guidance tied to component behavior and evidence.
Add public governance and support documentation without requiring adopters to read internal planning artifacts.
dimensions.nextAction: Build the stable docs IA around component reference pages, accessibility guidance, and public governance/support documentation.

dimensions.label: Visual QA matrix

benchmarkSignals.signal: Runs Storybook-based visual regression tests in CI and reviews screenshot diffs on pull requests.
Requires design review across component states and uses a component hardening/audit rubric as promotion evidence.
Publishes documented component states and foundations across a dedicated design-system site and preview environments.

dimensions.atom63Status: A limited homepage and DS-lab sanity pass is recorded. There is no complete, repeatable matrix for component states, viewports, themes, color schemes, focus, or reduced motion.
gaps: Cover the component gallery and stable candidates across mobile and desktop.
Cover light/dark, all supported themes, keyboard/focus states, and reduced motion.
Store reviewable evidence and define baseline-update ownership.
dimensions.nextAction: Define and execute a versioned visual QA matrix, then attach deterministic screenshots or approved visual-diff evidence.

dimensions.label: Release automation/provenance

benchmarkSignals.signal: Documents package grouping, versioning, source/dist contents, and a repeatable release process.
Uses explicit preview-to-stable lifecycle phases and automated change/release tooling.
Publishes release notes and migration guidance from a public package monorepo.

dimensions.atom63Status: A manual beta workflow has dry-run preflight, guardrails, an environment boundary, trusted-publisher intent, and npm provenance. Stable/latest dist-tag policy and a stable promotion workflow are not decided.
gaps: Resolve npm latest/dist-tag policy before stable promotion.
Define stable promotion, rollback, and registry verification steps.
Keep publish execution manually approved; this board is a dry-run guardrail only.
dimensions.nextAction: Approve the stable/latest dist-tag and rollback policy, then add a no-publish stable promotion preflight.

dimensions.label: Figma/design-tool parity gate

benchmarkSignals.signal: Distributes public Figma libraries whose components and variables are intended to match developer component implementations.
Provides component, style, and icon design resources alongside development resources from its getting-started path.
Links its Figma UI kit alongside Storybook and source code from the package documentation.

dimensions.atom63Status: Figma token output and token-surface audit artifacts exist, but variables sync, styleguide generation, component parity, and idempotent reruns have not completed manual QA.
gaps: Run and record variables sync and styleguide generation.
Prove an idempotent rerun with no unexpected design-file drift.
Define which stable components and variants require design-tool parity.
dimensions.nextAction: Execute the Figma manual QA packet, record idempotence evidence, and map stable code components to maintained design assets.

dimensions.label: Governance/support policy

benchmarkSignals.signal: Documents contribution scope, RFCs, decision authority, component lifecycle, conventions, and an evidence-based audit rubric.
Publishes contribution routes, issue reporting, accessibility guidance, and component documentation standards.
Encodes API conformance, testing expectations, preview lifecycle, and package change requirements in repository guidance and CI.

dimensions.atom63Status: Package boundaries, component review, beta support tiers, and named owner lanes are documented. Public contribution, maintenance, deprecation, security, browser-support, and support-response policies are incomplete.
gaps: Define maintainers and decision authority for stable API changes.
Publish deprecation, browser support, security reporting, and support-response policies.
Define the evidence and approval required to promote or retire a component.
dimensions.nextAction: Create a public governance and support policy with maintainers, compatibility scope, deprecation windows, security reporting, and promotion criteria.
